script.title: How an Army Defeated Itself in the Dark
sentences: An army of one hundred thousand defeated itself in the dark.
In September 1788, the Austrian army marched on Karánsebes to fight the Ottomans.
As night fell, scouting hussars reportedly bought schnapps and refused to share it.
A brawl started, and panic spread among soldiers speaking different languages.
Traditional accounts say officers shouted Halt, which non-German troops misheard as Allah.
Austrian artillery officers mistook their fleeing cavalry for an Ottoman attack and opened fire.
Emperor Joseph II fled in the chaos while his army destroyed itself.
Two days later, the Ottomans captured Karánsebes without engaging the Austrians.
script.description: The strange story of the Battle of Karánsebes in 1788.
claims_en: In September 1788, the Austrian army marched on Karánsebes during the Austro-Turkish War.
Austrian hussars reportedly bought schnapps from local Romanians and refused to share it with infantrymen.
A conflict erupted between hussars and infantry, creating panic among multi-ethnic Austrian forces.
Officers shouting 'Halt! Halt!' were misheard by non-German soldiers as 'Allah! Allah!'.
General of Artillery Colloredo ordered artillery fire believing fleeing hussars were an Ottoman cavalry charge.
Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II fled the chaotic scene.
The Ottoman army arrived two days later and captured Karánsebes without engaging the Austrians.
